concepts.why: The patient's presentation of neurological symptoms, elevated inflammatory markers, and imaging findings of extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface, along with the presence of a thick exudate in the subarachnoid space, are consistent with neurosarcoidosis.

The patient's history of relapsing neurological symptoms, such as aphasia, confusion, and right leg weakness, along with the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF and extensive white matter changes on MRI, are suggestive of multiple sclerosis.

The patient's high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody and the presence of a thick exudate in the subarachnoid space are consistent with rheumatoid meningitis, a rare complication of rheumatoid arthritis.

The patient's presentation of headache, right facial droop, and mild right nasolabial flattening, along with the imaging findings of extensive white matter changes, could be suggestive of CNS vasculitis, although the absence of vascular abnormalities on MRA and the lack of evidence of vasculitis on brain biopsy make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's history of relapsing neurological symptoms and the presence of extensive white matter changes on MRI are consistent with an inflammatory demyelinating disease, such as acute disseminated encephalomyelitis.
